source_name: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (public edition)
why_relevant: Europe-Region chapters define what CZ acquirers, issuers and merchants may do — acceptance obligations, contactless/CVM limits, Click to Pay, central acquiring. Rule changes are leading indicators of CZ market-structure shifts.

source_name: Mastercard Rules (public rulebook, Chapter 13 Europe Region)
why_relevant: Chapter 13 covers Europe-Region licensing and central acquiring, which governs how non-CZ acquirers can serve Czech merchants — a structural driver of the CZ acceptance market that no local source states explicitly.

source_name: Mastercard Economics Institute / SpendingPulse insight reports
why_relevant: MEI publishes country-level retail-spend growth forecasts and ticket-size behaviour that name Czechia explicitly (e.g. CZ among strongest forecast growth in CEE); derived from scheme transaction data, so it precedes official statistics.

source_name: Visa Consulting & Analytics – Business and Economic Insights / Spending Momentum Index
why_relevant: Visa's economics arm publishes spend-momentum and consumer-payment-attitude series; CEE/CZ cuts appear in regional editions and feed the CZ press releases, giving methodology context for the numbers Visa quotes locally.

source_name: Visa corporate newsroom (global) — corporate.visa.com
why_relevant: Global/European Visa announcements (e.g. Visa Intelligent Authorisation rollout in Europe) that are subsequently localised for CZ; gives the earliest sight of product/pricing changes that will reach the Czech market.

source_name: American Express Česká republika – country site (acceptance & cardholder pages)
why_relevant: Amex is a three-party scheme whose CZ footprint is narrow and shifting (acceptance handed to Global Payments Europe in 2013; consumer-card issuance wound down). The country site documents which products and acceptance arrangements still exist in CZ.

source_name: Diners Club CS – akceptace karty Diners Club
why_relevant: Documents the CZ status of the Diners Club / Discover / PULSE acceptance network after the Austrian owner ended CZ/SK/PL issuing in August 2022 — the reference point for whether the brand persists as acceptance-only in Czechia.

source_name: UnionPay International – Media/News Center (Czech Republic items)
why_relevant: UnionPay publishes hard CZ acceptance counts that nobody else does — merchant numbers accepting UPI, ATM-acceptance percentages, named bank ATM networks (ČSOB, Česká spořitelna, KB, Euronet, MONETA) and the Global Payments Europe acquiring deal.

source_name: ČSOB acquiring – merchant manual for card acceptance (platbakartou.csob.cz)
why_relevant: Acquirer merchant manuals enumerate which scheme brands are actually accepted on CZ terminals (Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, Diners/Discover, JCB, UnionPay, Amex) and the scheme rules as operationalised locally — a ground-truth read on scheme presence in CZ acceptance.

source_name: Kurzy.cz / e15 / Retail News – Czech business media relaying scheme statistics
why_relevant: Czech financial media reproduce scheme figures with numbers intact (e.g. Visa-issued CZ card turnover passing CZK 1 trillion; share of Mastercard payments that are contactless; mobile as the most-used payment method), and often quote scheme country managers on market share — data points that vanish from scheme sites over time.

source_name: Discover Global Network (Diners Club International / PULSE) acceptance in CZ
why_relevant: After Diners Club issuing ended in CZ/SK/PL, acceptance for Diners Club International, Discover and PULSE continues through Discover Global Network partnerships with local payment institutions — this is the pointer to who now carries the brand in Czechia.

source_name: GoPay blog – history of payment cards in Czechia (scheme milestone chronology)
why_relevant: Consolidates scheme entry dates and acceptance milestones in the Czech market (first card payments, contactless launch in June 2011, brand arrivals) — useful for dating scheme-level structural changes when the schemes' own archives have been pruned.

source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků systému CERTIS (PDF, versioned)
why_relevant: Versioned register of direct CERTIS participants (banks, branches, credit unions, payment/e-money institutions) with bank codes. Version numbering enables change tracking of rail membership over time.

source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků okamžitých plateb (instant payments participants, PDF)
why_relevant: Definitive list of CERTIS participants joined to the Czech instant-payment scheme — the adoption/coverage baseline for okamžité platby, unavailable in international datasets.

source_name: ČNB – Číselníky, seznamy, registry (účty a kódy bank)
why_relevant: Machine-readable code lists (bank codes, BIC, IBAN structures) needed to join CERTIS/instant-payment/card datasets to institutions; the canonical CZ actor identifier registry.

source_name: ČNB – Seznam institucí relevantních pro statistiku platebního styku (PSRI)
source_subtype: reporting population list / release calendar entry
why_relevant: Defines the reporting population for CZ payment statistics (banks, credit unions, payment institutions, e-money institutions, small-scale providers) — key for knowing who must report and therefore who publishes data.

source_name: ČNB Lab – Payments research stream
why_relevant: ČNB research/innovation lab output on payment behaviour, instant payments and cash usage — analytical context and occasionally granular datasets not in headline statistics.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace – Standard ČBA č. 26 (QR kódy / QR Platba)
why_relevant: Authoritative CZ QR-payment standard document (format for sharing CZK payment data via QR codes) issued by the banking association — the normative basis of QR Platba/SPAYD.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) – official site / standards & statistics
why_relevant: Industry body maintaining banking standards (incl. QR Platba), publishing sector statistics, analyses and member lists; a primary pointer to further CZ payments actors and documents.

source_name: QR Platba – oficiální stránka standardu
why_relevant: Public home of the QR Platba / SPAYD (Short Payment Descriptor) specification, adoption information and implementation guidance — the CZ-specific QR payment structure invisible in international data.

source_name: Komerční banka – Klientský formát pro QR platbu (bank implementation spec)
why_relevant: Bank-level implementation of the ČBA QR standard; shows which optional SPAYD attributes a major scheme-rail bank supports and how the standard evolves in practice.

source_name: Bank iD (Bankovní identita, a.s.) – newsroom & adoption statistics
why_relevant: Operator of the Czech bank-based e-ID scheme; publishes user counts, transaction/verification volumes, use-case splits and bank coverage — the core uptake metric for national bank e-ID rails.

source_name: Informační web elektronické identity / Národní bod (NIA, identita.gov.cz)
why_relevant: State national identification/authentication node (NIA) that Bank iD federates into; documents accepted identity means, connected service providers and publishes usage information — the public-sector side of e-ID adoption.

source_name: Digitální a informační agentura (DIA) / MV ČR – e-identity usage releases
why_relevant: Agency and ministry communications report eIdentita login counts, growth rates and which state portals drive volume — corroborates Bank iD's own figures from the state side.

source_name: Global Payments Europe / Global Payments s.r.o. (CZ) – processor & acquirer
why_relevant: Successor of MUZO, historically the dominant CZ card-transaction processor and a major acquirer (JV with Erste); corporate news and product pages reveal terminal estate, processing scope and portfolio moves.

source_name: Worldline Česká republika (Cataps s.r.o., ex-KB acquiring)
why_relevant: Second major CZ acquirer/processor (carve-out of Komerční banka's merchant business); local pages plus group results give CZ merchant-acceptance and terminal-fleet indications.

source_name: Komerční banka – výroční a pololetní zprávy / investor reporting
why_relevant: Bank-level rail metrics: KB+ digital-bank client counts, transaction and channel statistics disclosed in annual/quarterly reporting — bottom-up validation of scheme and instant-payment adoption.

source_name: European Payments Council – Register of Participants (SCT Inst, SEPA schemes)
why_relevant: Downloadable register showing which Czech PSPs adhere to SCT Inst and other SEPA schemes — links the domestic CERTIS instant rail to the euro-area instant rail and to Verification of Payee obligations.
